mechanisms.description: A later executive order revoked, rescinded or expressly superseded the member in full, naming it by number. The revoking order may belong to any family; the project holds each revoking text used here, and none qualifies the revocation by tract, section or "in part".
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of the revoking order (fixed per branch).

mechanisms.description: The order withdrew lands "until" a stated date in aid of pending legislation. Eight of the nine orders also say the lands would then become subject to disposal without further order; Executive Order 2542-A states only the date, and the clause appears in its extension, Executive Order 2896.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The stated date in the order (or in a held extension order), fixed per branch.

mechanisms.description: Coordinator ruling P1: an order whose only operative content revokes another order, excludes land from a forest and restores it to the general land laws, or opens to entry land already excluded, does one thing and does it on issue. Its consequence (the other order's end, the land's new status) belongs to the other order's lifecycle or the land's history. A restoration that keeps a reversion, retained tract, reserved right or purpose restriction is not only a restoration and stays open.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The order's effective date; where the order's own terms fix a later opening (a preference period, a settlement date, the date the land becomes subject to general disposition), the date of the last step those terms fix.

mechanisms.description: Coordinator ruling P2 (owner decision D-20261021-strike-and-insert): an order whose only operative content amends, corrects or extends another order or proclamation has no command of its own after issue; its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends, and the parent's lifecycle carries it.

Administrative-site, classification, resurvey and pending-legislation withdrawals made under the Pickett Act have no built-in end and remain in force until revoked by the President or Congress; FLPMA (1976) repealed the authority but saved existing withdrawals (an authority repeal, which under ruling P3 is not an end). Persistence on 2026-10-14 still needs a current land record.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: None: an end needs a revocation (later executive order or public land order) or statute reaching the land.

mechanisms.description: Orders that create a forest from parts of others, transfer land between forests, merge one forest into another, add land, rename a forest or redraw its boundaries are operative acts on land whose designation persists; they are not pure textual amendments, so ruling P2 does not reach them. Each ends only when a later order or statute names it, or expressly redescribes the forest's whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions (ruling P3). NFMA (1976) bars return of land still reserved as national forest to the public domain except by Act of Congress; that is context, not a current-law predicate.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: None until a later instrument reaching the member is held.

mechanisms.description: A Public Land Order of the Secretary of the Interior (1942 on) revoked the member in full, as the official BLM Table of Public Land Orders states it: the row names the member by number and says "revoking" with no "in part" qualifier for that order. The PLO texts are not held.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The PLO signature date as the BLM table gives it (fixed per branch); the Federal Register publication date may be the effective date.

mechanisms.description: Coordinator ruling P7: a later instrument abolished by name, or merged by name all the lands of, the one national forest that the member constituted or named, and constituting or naming that forest was the member's only operative content.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date the abolishing or merging instrument fixes (fixed per branch).

lead.basis: The order excludes land and provides that it "shall be restored to the public domain and become subject to settlement ... on such date and after such notice by publication as the Secretary of the Interior may prescribe", with entry thirty days later. procedure.description: Creates a forest from parts of others, transfers land between forests, merges forests, adds land, renames a forest, or redraws its boundary (including mixed orders that also exclude land).

lead.basis: The order is an operative act on land whose forest designation persists, not a pure textual amendment, so ruling P2 does not reach it; it ends only when a later order or statute names it or expressly redescribes the forest's whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions, and no such instrument is held.

gaps: The Forest Service chronological record mapping this order to the named forest's later actions (consolidation, renaming, redescription), with the text of each later instrument to test whether it names this order or expressly redescribes the whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions.
For a persistence lead: the current Land Areas Report showing the forest or name on 2026-10-14. 16 U.S.C. 1609(a) is context only.

Where the forest the order constituted was later abolished or merged by name but the order also assigned land to another forest (for example EO 870, Holy Cross and Leadville, Holy Cross abolished by PLO 263; EO 801, Pocatello and Cache, Pocatello merged by EO 2179), ruling P7 does not reach it and the lead stays open.

Classification, resurvey, exchange and pending-legislation withdrawals without a stated end: need the later Act, proclamation or revocation for the land.
Reservations for Indian, military or other-agency purposes: need later instruments for the land; named overlap families PD-INDIAN, PD-MILITARY-RESERVATION, PD-LAND-WITHDRAWAL.
